full_judgment:
Md Iftikhar Rasool J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 13-4-1995 passed by the Additional District Judge, Chandpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1992 affirming the judgment and order dated 9-3-1992 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 allowing the pre-emption Case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that opposite party No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act of 1949 against the petitioners and others in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur for pre-emption of the disputed land transferred by opposite party Nos. 4-11 by four different kabalas, two of which were registered on 22-1-1981 and the rest two on 24-1-1981 for total consideration of Taka 1,11,000.00 without serving any notice upon the opposite party No. 1 as per section 23 of the said Act. In the pre-emption application opposite party No. 1 stated that he was the youngest son of his father having been born on 16-5-1969 and attaining majority on 16-5-1987. It is further stated by opposite party No. 1 in the pre-emption application that he was entitled to file the pre-emption case within three years from the date of attainment of majority as per the provisions of section 6 of the Limitation Act and that he came to know of the disputed kabalas from Md Salamatullah Khan and Habibur Rahman and thereafter taking certified copies of the disputed kabalas he definitely came to know of the transfer on 13-5-1990. It is further stated by opposite party No. 1 in the pre-emption application that on 24-3-1978 and 19-9-1978 some lands and share of the disputed building belonging to his deceased father were transferred by way of forgery and false personification and the said two deeds were registered with the District Registrar's Officer at Comilla for declaration of those two kabalas as collusive, fraudulent and forged, Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 was filed in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Chandpur. Opposite Party No. 1 coming to know of the disputed kabalas transferring the disputed land and the share of disputed building in favour of the present petitioners by opposite party Nos. 4-11, the opposite party No. 1 instituted the instant Miscellaneous case upon deposit of the amount of the consideration money of Taka 1,11,000.00 together with the statutory compensation at the rate of 5%. 

 3. The petitioners as opposite party Nos. 1-3 in the instant miscellaneous case contested the same by filing a joint written objection wherein they denied all material allegations made in the application and staying, inter alia, that the case is barred by limitation and that the actual name of opposite party No. 1 is Jinnat Ali Bhuiyan and using such name Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 was filed by him. The entire interest of opposite party No. 1 (i.e. the pre-emptor) in the land as well as in the building has been transferred by two registered kabalas dated 24-3-78 and 19-9-78 and that the interest of opposite party No.1 in the disputed holding having been transferred and he having no subsisting interest in the disputed holding, he cannot maintain the miscellaneous case for pre-emption and, as such, the pre-emption case instituted by opposite party No. 1 is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. During trial of the case the petitioner (i.e. opposite party No. 1) examined 5 PWs as against 4 OPWs and thereafter the trial Court allowed the miscellaneous case filed by opposite party No. 1 by his judgment and order dated 9-3-1992. Against said judgment and order the petitioners as appellants filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1992 before the District Judge, Chandpur and the said appeal was transferred to the Court of the Additional District Judge, Chandpur who after hearing dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and order passed by the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order by the Additional District Judge, Chandpur on 13-4-1995 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1992 the petitioners moved this Court under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule. Opposite Party No. 1 has opposed the Rule. 

 6. It is admitted that the present petitioners as appellants filed FMA No. 52 of 1992 against the judgment and order dated 9-3-1992 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur allowing the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. It is seen that the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case was instituted by the opposite party No. 1 for pre-emption of some lands of the disputed holding and share of building transferred to the present petitioners by co-sharer opposite party Nos. 4-11 on the basis of registered kabalas dated 22- 3-1979, 17-8-1979, 7-4-1979,11-4-1979 and 14-4-1979. It is noticed that in the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 the present opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor set up the case almost on identical lines as he set up in the instant Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990. He claimed that he was a minor at the time of transfer of the disputed land and share in the building and he attained majority on 16-5-1987. It was his further case in the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 that he came to know of the transfers made by opposite party Nos. 4-11 from Salamatullah Khan and Habibur Rahman for the first time on 10-5-1990. A Division Bench of this Court by judgment and order dated 23-2-1998 dismissed the appeal filed by the present petitioners and affirmed the judgment and order of the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur. Against the judgment and order of the Division Bench of this Court the present petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 585 of 1998 before the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division by their judgment and order dated 9-12-1998 were pleased to dismiss the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal. So, it appears that Appellate Division upheld the observations and findings of the High Court Division on all counts including the questions of limitation and minority of the opposite party No. 1 at the relevant time of the transfers made by opposite party Nos. 4 to 11 in favour of the petitioners. Paradoxically enough the petitioners while contesting Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 and the instant Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 did not make any attempt for staying the proceedings of these two miscellaneous cases, till disposal of Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 and there is no material before us to show that any attempt to this effect was ever made by the present petitioners before the trial Court. The petitioners as appellants in FMA No. 52 of 1992 also did not make any prayer for staying the proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 till disposal of Title Suit No. 117 of 1986. 

 7. Mr Syed Mohammad Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, argues that this Court in its revisional jurisdiction can stay proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 till disposal of Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 after setting aside the judgments and orders passed by the lower appellate Court and the trial Court and this will meet the ends of justice. 

 8. Mr MA Wahab Mia, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 contends that the above submission of the learned lawyer of the petitioners is not tenable and if such plea is accepted then this Court will have to by-pass the judgment and order of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 585 of 1998 which arose out of Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990. It is submitted by Mr MA Wahab Mia, the learned Counsel for opposite party No. 1 that factually and legally both the courts below concurred with each other and this Court in its revisional jurisdiction will not interfere with the concurred findings of both the Courts below unless there is gross and palpable illegality committed by those courts. He further contends that when the petitioners did not pray for stay of the proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 and Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 till disposal of Title Suit No. 117 of 1986, the petitioners will be deemed to have given a go-by to this plea. 

 9. We have given our anxious consideration to this submissions made by the learned lawyers of both the parties. On the question of limitation which is mixed question of law as well as of fact, the petitioners have not been able to place any material before us to show that opposite party No. 1 had any knowledge of the disputed kabalas four in number before 13-5-1990. There is also no material before us that any notice of the disputed transfer as required under section 23 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act was served upon the opposite party No. 1. Section 24 of the said Act provides that if no notice under section 23 is issued or served upon the petitioner (opposite party No. 1 in the instant case) he can file a case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the disputed land within four months from the date of knowledge of the transfer. In the instant case the opposite party No. 1 has specifically stated that he filed the case within four months from the date of his knowledge of the disputed transfer. This being the position, the present case appears to have been filed within four months from the date of knowledge of the disputed transfer. The plea of the petitioners is, that the proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 may be stayed till disposal of Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 after setting aside the judgment and orders of both the Courts below. We have already held that the findings of both the Courts below being concurrent we find no cogent legal ground to set aside those two judgments and orders. The fate of this case is linked with the fate of Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990. The petitioners having failed in FMA No. 52 of 1992 as well as in the Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 585 of 1998 there is no scope for staying the proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1990 till disposal of Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 after setting aside the judgment and orders of the Courts below. 

 10. In the background of the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above we find no substance in this Rule. The Rule is accordingly discharged without any order as to costs. Stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.
